## 🔗 Safer link routing

- **Keep functional query parameters intact.** Query cleanup preserves unknown parameters, including search terms, OAuth callback data, pagination and download options. Recognized signed links stay unchanged. Extra share-tag cleanup applies only to supported Instagram and YouTube URL shapes.
- **Preserve the meaning of supported links.** BreezeWiki and Phantom keep the Fandom wiki name, Wikiless receives the Wikipedia language, Invidious converts YouTube short and live links to watch URLs, and OpenStreetMap receives supported coordinates, searches and coordinate-to-coordinate directions. Unsupported URL shapes follow the service’s fallback preference.
- **Inspect before opening.** Home and Android’s share menu can show the incoming, cleaned and alternative links, removed parameter names, and the selected target. Open the previewed destination, choose a different app for this link, or open the original once. Shared messages with multiple links can be cleaned selectively while preserving the surrounding text.

## 🧭 More routing control

- Choose a browser or compatible app per service or domain, including an app chooser on each opening. An unavailable app falls back to Android’s chooser.
- Choose whether an unavailable alternative opens the original site, asks first, or blocks automatic fallback. The setup check and diagnostics distinguish app selection, handoff and in-app WebView outcomes.
- Create domain rules to preserve specific parameters or skip individual cleanup operations. Preview the changes before applying the **Balanced**, **Strict**, or **Clean only** routing profile.
- Turn routing on or off from Home, or pause for 15 minutes, an hour, or until you resume it. Use the setup check to review the browser role, Android’s link defaults and the delivery stages of an example link.
- Instance checks classify HTTP failures and show the response status. Fastest uses fresh measurements and skips cooldowns. Hosted frontends can use a personal HTTPS instance even when the public list is empty.

## 🛡️ Private browsing and downloads

- Child and pop-up tabs inherit their private session. WebViews without isolated profile support show an explanation when you try to open a private tab. New private sessions use fresh profiles.
- Private download records stay out of the saved index and disappear when the session ends. Transfers already in progress can finish, and saved files remain in their storage location.
- Download cookies and referrers stay within their origin through URL cleanup and HTTP redirects. HTTP resume checks the validator and byte range and restarts from the beginning when the server returns a changed entity or invalid range.

## 🗂️ Browser, backups and diagnostics

- Set the history limit and automatic tab age in Settings. Site settings show effective global values until a site override is applied. Compatible WebViews can clear data for the current site, and a renderer loss can be recovered from the affected tab.
- Bookmarks keep a canonical source when it is known and use current routing preferences on reopen. Picture-in-picture uses a 16:9 default and clamps other aspect ratios to Android’s accepted range.
- Export selected settings, custom rules and bookmarks, or share a service rule package. The import review shows rule conflicts and rejected items. You can edit, duplicate and preview custom routing rules locally.
- Prepare a diagnostic report with reproduction steps, expected and actual behavior, and an optional URL. Review it before sharing. Automatic diagnostic links are reduced to their hosts.

## ✅ Verification and installation

The Android workflow checks the exact release commit with JVM tests, static analysis, API compatibility checks, Android lint, debug and minified builds, reproducibility checks, and connected tests on API 28 and API 36. The release workflow signs the APK and smoke-tests its bundled routing manifest.

Download `libredirect-mobile-v1.3.14.apk` and its companion SHA-256 checksum from the assets below. Android 8.0 and later are supported. Private browsing and site-only data removal depend on the installed WebView provider.

[Full changelog](https://github.com/sametcn99/libredirect-mobile/compare/v1.3.13...v1.3.14)
